newsitem.title: USA: HORSE RACING-CAPTAIN BODGIT FORCED TO RETIRE WITH LEG INJURY.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-CAPTAIN BODGIT FORCED TO RETIRE WITH LEG INJURY.

text.p: Captain Bodgit, who loomed as a serious threat to Silver Charm's bid for the Triple Crown at the Belmont Stakes, was retired Wednesday after suffering a strained tendon in his left front leg during the Preakness.
Captain Bodgit, winner of seven races in 12 career starts, was third at the Preakness just two heads behind Silver Charm after finishing second to him in a photo finish at the Kentucky Derby.
Although the horse shows no signs of pain, the Team Valour syndicate, which owns Captain Bodgit, decided to retire him.
"He has a strain in the tendon," said Team Valour president Barry Irwin from his Pasadena, California, office.
"(Trainer) Gary Capuano noticed some swelling two days after the race. It looked better yesterday, but an ultrasonic scan showed there was a core lesion."

Irwin indicated the decision to retire Captain Bodgit was precautionary. Running him in the June 7 Belmont Stakes, the last leg of the Triple Crown races, would subject the horse to greater injury, he said.
At the Derby, Captain Bodgit put on a furious run down the backstretch and nearly caught Silver Charm from behind.
Last Saturday's Preakness was nearly a repeat after Silver Charm edged past Free House down the stretch at Pimlico.
Again, Captain Bodgit closed with such force that Silver Charm felt enough of his presence for one last push to hold on and win.
"He doesn't even know he's injured," said Capuano. "He's in no pain, he jogs around and is ready to go again right now. That's him."
The brilliant Captain Bodgit has never finished worse than third in a race. Besides his seven victories, he also has finished second once and third four times.
